newsitem.title: USA: DuPont posts record earnings per share.
newsitem.headline: DuPont posts record earnings per share.

text.p: DuPont Co. Wednesday reported record fourth-quarter and full-year 1996 earnings per share, led by gains in its petroleum and chemicals and specialities businesses.

Profits rose to $858 million, or a record $1.52 a share, in the quarter ended Dec. 31 from $627 million, or $1.13 a share, in the year-ago period. Sales rose 10 percent to $11.4 billion from $10.4 billion.
For full-year 1996, earnings rose 10 percent to $3.6 billion, or $6.47 per share, from $3.3 billion, or $5.61 per share, in 1995. Sales edged up 4 percent to $43.8 billion from $42.2 billion.
"Upstream petroleum results increased 46 percent to $706 million and were a major contributor to our earnings growth," President and CEO John Krol said in a statement.
"In addition, we have taken a number of significant steps toward strengthening and positioning our business portfolio for profitable growth."
Petroleum segment earnings were $901 million, up $237 million, or 36 percent, and the second highest in the history of DuPont's Conoco unit, it said.
Earnings from refined petroleum products rose 7 percent to $195 million as margins improved.

Krol said DuPont had regained financial flexibility by essentially completing repayment of the $8 billion of debt incurred in 1995 to redeem shares from Seagram Co. Ltd. and by repurchasing for $500 million the 156 million warrants issued to Seagram.

"The double-digit chemicals and specialities volume growth in the fourth quarter gives us momentum moving into the new year," he said. "Petroleum is also well positioned, given major refinery upgrades completed in 1996 and reasonably strong upstream market conditions."
DuPont's stock was unchanged at $104.375 on the New York Stock Exchange in late morning trading.
